newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak government suspends referendum preparations.
newsitem.headline: Slovak government suspends referendum preparations.

text.p: The Slovak government said on Tuesday preparations for a referendum on direct presidental elections had been suspended pending a challenge before the Constitutional Court.
Deputy premier Katarina Tothova told reporters the cabinet had asked the court to rule whether the constitution could in fact be changed by a referendum.
President Michal Kovac last month set two referendums for May 23 and 24, one on the election and the other on whether Slovakia should join NATO. There was no mention of any impact on the NATO vote.

The NATO referendum was called by Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's ruling parliamentary majority, while the poll proposing direct election of the president resulted from a petition initiated by the opposition.
The opposition referendum is an attempt to prevent Meciar assuming presidential powers when Kovac's term of office expires next March.

In its present composition the Slovak parliament would be unable to muster the necessary two-thirds majority to elect a new president, which would mean presidential powers would be delegated to the government, effectively to Meciar.
